chunks: Take instruction from how Allah’s wrath, violence, chastisement and punishment fell upon the arrogant nations before you. Take admonition from the resting places of their cheeks and their bodies, and seek Allah’s protection from the dangers of pride, as you seek His protection from calamities.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ: The arrogant, those who display pride and haughtiness
key_terms.طَوَارِقِ الدَّهْرِ: Calamities or sudden misfortunes of time
key_terms.لَوَاقِحِ الْكِبْرِ: The dangers/essence of pride (literally the 'wombs' or sources of pride)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of seeking protection from pride in Shia teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs vivid imagery of the 'hollowed cheeks' and 'fallen flanks' of past arrogant nations to illustrate the tangible consequences of divine retribution, a motif deeply resonant in Shia exegesis of historical decline. This warning against *al-kibr* (pride) is framed not merely as a moral failing but as a spiritual vulnerability requiring the same urgent supplication as protection from sudden worldly calamities (*tawariq al-dahr*).
